critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext.refresh() correctly guards against a late stale /auth/me response clobbering an already-logged-in user (setUser((prev) => (prev && prev.portal ? prev : false))). Good pattern.
server.py is 932 lines — consider splitting into routers per resource (auth/ops/business/partner) for maintainability.
Frontend correctly uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL and Authorization: Bearer fallback (localStorage 'sawari_token') given the httpOnly cookie may be dropped in preview envs.
CORS_ORIGINS is set to '*' but withCredentials=true on the axios client. If backend uses `allow_credentials=True` with '*', browsers will refuse cookies — verify explicit origin allowlist for prod.

rca of the issue: Reported issue: OPS dashboard stays on a blank blue-gradient loader after login. RCA finding: NOT REPRODUCIBLE. Login POST /api/auth/login returned 200 → setToken + setUser executed → HashRouter route /#/ops mounted OpsPortal → GET /api/ops/dashboard (200), GET /api/cabs (200), GET /api/activity (200) → dashboard rendered with KPI cards and admin-slot-visualiser-grid within ~2s. No console errors, no React errors, no failed network calls. Most likely earlier report was caused by: (a) preview env dropping the httpOnly cookie AND browser blocking localStorage (then /auth/me returns 401 → user set to false → LoginScreen shown), OR (b) transient backend restart during login. The current code already handles (a) by storing token in localStorage and sending Bearer, and by not clobbering already-logged-in user on late /auth/me failure. Mitigation: none required at code level; ensure preview URL uses same domain (it does).
